Optional ondisc boundary contract

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-tools-hardening-ondisc-contract.Rmd
contributor-tools-hardening-ondisc-contract.Rmd

Contributing · Object model · Discovery walkthrough · Object fields

SCEPTRE’s in-memory path does not load ondisc. Backed paths inspect actual capabilities before creating/reopening files or executing native count operations. A successful check establishes the required R/class/native interface, not a new numerical or platform qualification. Package version alone is never acceptance. Checks are cached only for the loaded namespace in the current R process.

Upstream status checked on 2026-10-19

Authenticated gh api reads of the official upstream repository found:

  • main is 589803edea2a66ad15e7f07186bee16c7739ab8c, the pair-iteration bounds fix, with package version 1.3.5.
  • The GitHub releases expose only v1.1 and v1.2.0; v1.2.0 resolves to 5e5e4e55f407ff9025e8ec1c5f84c992b341e2fd.
  • The pinned NAMESPACE exports the public matrix/CellRanger constructors, backing-file reader, example writer and S4 methods. It does not export the required pair/group/threshold operations or the constructor accepting a shared import ID.
  • The public matrix constructor forwards to an internal constructor whose default integer_id is zero. Its exported formals do not let SCEPTRE supply the shared ID.

Thus the inspected official upstream API still leaves a support/distribution gap: there is no discovered supported released replacement for the private contract below. This is scoped to the official GitHub source/releases inspected, not a claim about a new release, a Bioconductor ruling, or an upstream commitment. No upstream contacts or library upgrades were performed.

The recommended source remains the exact README/CI pin above. Earlier project qualification identified a same-version 1.3.5 source without the pair bounds fix, so Version: 1.3.5 cannot replace a source pin. The local installation used for this hardening test is separately ondisc 1.2.0, R 4.6.0/macOS arm64, with no RemoteSha in DESCRIPTION. It passed the interface gate and the existing backed semantic regressions; its version does not prove it is that pinned source. No new installed-package qualification of upstream main or another release is claimed here.

Required operations

R/ondisc_capabilities.R is the executable interface manifest. It verifies the following function argument lists, the exported reader, the required odm slots, and registered native arities. Private calls remain confined to storage.

Operation Required entry Required semantics
Create counts private create_odm_from_r_matrix_internal(mat, file_to_write, chunk_size, compression_level, integer_id) Preserve supplied shared integer ID; row-accessible counts, feature order and integer-conversion behavior. The response and guide stores share the caller’s import ID.
Reopen exported initialize_odm_from_backing_file(odm_file) Create a process-local handle and expose saved dimensions, feature IDs and import ID. Both file IDs must match before use.
Row read odm row [ method, registered load_row_cpp Full gene row in original column order, followed by SCEPTRE selection in requested source order; repeats remain repeats.
Assignment threshold private threshold_count_matrix_cpp Original one-based stored positions; ondisc coerces count/threshold to integers. Stored zeros can pass threshold zero; unstored zeros never appear.
Pair counts private compute_n_ok_pairs_ondisc Count stored positions in treatment/control groups for requested rows; selected-cell and NT coordinate rules remain unchanged.
Pair + NT summary private compute_nt_nonzero_matrix_and_n_ok_pairs_ondisc Same pair counts plus NT-group-by-gene counts and totals, including supplied group overlaps.
Group counts private compute_n_trt_cells_matrix_ondisc Preserve group order, requested response order/repeats, dimensions and supplied membership multiplicity.

Required raw odm slots are h5_file: character, dimension: integer, feature_ids: character, ptr: externalptr, and integer_id: integer. The typed SCEPTRE BackedCountStore remains independent of ondisc at package load: its descriptor is the sole saved authority and its optional handle is process local. Public count getters reconstruct the existing raw odm view; numerical kernels and per-gene count paths are unchanged.

SCEPTRE owns copies of group-coordinate vectors before calling native routines that decrement them in place. It sorts pair requests for reading, restores original request order afterward, and appends an inert n_genes + 1 request to keep legacy native lookahead within bounds. The sentinel is never read as a gene, never enlarges the statistical family, and its unused output is discarded. These safeguards remain even when a compatible installation includes the bounds fix. This change introduces no alternate count kernel, RNG consumption or CRT support for ondisc.

Saved-object and content lifecycle

The backing descriptor contains absolute path, file MD5, dimensions, feature IDs and shared integer ID. The ID establishes pairing, not immutable content. Saving/reopening verifies the anchored checksum; verified path relocation does not invalidate compatible fits/results. Public backed saving stores closed handles. readRDS() alone permits descriptor and saved-result inspection but cannot execute count-dependent work; the public backed reader opens current process handles. See the read/write help for runnable save/read examples.

Active backing files are immutable. Getters and per-pair loops do not scan full files to detect unsupported external edits. Changed count content/import summaries require reimport. A capability failure explains the installed version, missing or changed operations, qualified source pin, restart requirement and availability of the independent memory path; it occurs before creating count files. Checking capabilities cannot prove that arbitrary new native code keeps these semantic promises: qualification against these tests remains necessary.

Regression evidence and remaining qualification

  • test-ondisc-capabilities.R: compatible API independent of version text; missing operation, incompatible class, missing exported reader, changed reader formals/native arity; actionable absent/incompatible diagnostics; failure before files are created; installed API acceptance.
  • test-refactor-storage.R: stored-zero/fraction differences, row/column ordering, owned native coordinates, sentinel behavior, group counts and shared-ID save/reopen checks.
  • test-schema-migration.R: typed closed stores, relocation/tamper rejection, metadata-only descriptor methods, legacy migration and saved results.
  • test-refactor-contracts.R: actual backed import/QC/save/reopen/discovery agreement with sparse workflows and wrong-file-ID rejection.

Incompatible-install tests use injected metadata snapshots, not suspect native code or replacement packages in the ordinary library. The cold-process probe loads the package, migrates an in-memory fixture, and inspects a closed typed store without loading ondisc. No broad platform, R-floor, backend CRT or new upstream-release qualification follows from these local checks.
